spec: Build a notification hub. Services publish events to a central SNS topic; subscribers register through a REST API choosing a channel (email-like or webhook-like), and each channel is backed by its own SQS queue subscribed to the topic. Subscriptions are stored in DynamoDB, and an endpoint reports how many messages each channel queue has received.

complexity.rationale: Topic-to-channel fan-out requires subscription management, routing, and delivery observation.

congruence_checklist: Per-channel SQS queues subscribed to the topic
Publish endpoint pushing events to the topic

plan.summary: A FastAPI notification hub service. Producer services POST events to the hub, which publishes them to a central SNS topic. Subscribers are registered through a REST API and choose a delivery channel ('email' or 'webhook'); each channel is backed by its own SQS queue that is subscribed to the SNS topic. Subscription records are persisted in DynamoDB, and a stats endpoint reports per-channel queue message counts read from SQS queue attributes. The service runs as a standalone process and calls SNS, SQS and DynamoDB directly with boto3.

endpoints.purpose: Liveness/readiness probe reporting reachability of SNS, SQS and DynamoDB dependencies.
Publish an event to the central SNS topic (subject, event_type and JSON payload); returns the SNS message id and generated event id.
Register a subscriber with a channel ('email' or 'webhook') and destination target; stores the record in DynamoDB and returns the created subscription.
List subscriptions, optionally filtered by channel via query parameter.
Fetch a single subscription by id from DynamoDB.
Update a subscription's target, event_types filter or active flag.
Delete a subscription record from DynamoDB.
List the supported channels and their backing SQS queue URLs.
Report per-channel message counts (visible, in-flight, delayed) read from SQS queue attributes for every channel queue.
Receive (and optionally delete) pending messages from that channel's SQS queue so operators and tests can inspect fan-out results.

data_models.name: Subscription
fields: target: str (email address or webhook URL)
event_types: list[str] (empty list means all events)

data_models.name: ChannelStats
fields: total_received: int (sum of the three counters)

aws_resources.name: notification-hub-events-topic
aws_resources.justification: Central topic that POST /events publishes to; the fan-out point for all channel queues.

aws_resources.name: notification-hub-email-queue
aws_resources.justification: Per-channel queue for the email-like channel, subscribed to the SNS topic; read by GET /channels/stats and GET /channels/email/messages.

aws_resources.name: notification-hub-webhook-queue
aws_resources.justification: Per-channel queue for the webhook-like channel, subscribed to the SNS topic; read by GET /channels/stats and GET /channels/webhook/messages.

aws_resources.name: notification-hub-dlq
aws_resources.justification: Shared dead-letter queue configured as redrive target for both channel queues so undeliverable messages are retained rather than lost.

aws_resources.name: notification-hub-topic-subscriptions
aws_resources.justification: SNS-to-SQS subscriptions (raw message delivery) binding each channel queue to the topic; this is the fan-out mechanism the spec requires.

aws_resources.name: notification-hub-subscriptions
aws_resources.justification: Stores subscriber records for the /subscriptions CRUD endpoints; partition key subscription_id with a channel-created_at GSI to support listing by channel.

aws_resources.name: notification-hub-service-role
aws_resources.justification: Role/policy granting the standalone backend sns:Publish, sqs:GetQueueAttributes/ReceiveMessage/DeleteMessage and DynamoDB CRUD on only the planned resources.

aws_resources.name: notification-hub-queue-policies
aws_resources.justification: SQS queue policies allowing the SNS topic to deliver messages into each channel queue.

aws_resources.name: /notification-hub/application
aws_resources.justification: Log group the service writes structured publish/subscription/stats logs to for operational visibility.

assumptions: Exactly two channels are supported, 'email' and 'webhook', each mapped to one dedicated SQS queue; unknown channel values are rejected with HTTP 422.

'How many messages each channel queue has received' is interpreted as the SQS ApproximateNumberOfMessages* attributes summed into a total_received figure, since Community Edition LocalStack exposes queue attributes but not durable per-queue delivery counters.
The hub only publishes and reports; it does not itself deliver email or call webhook URLs, so no outbound delivery worker (and therefore no Lambda or API Gateway) is planned.
Subscription registration stores the subscriber record in DynamoDB and associates it with the pre-provisioned channel queue; it does not create a new SNS subscription per subscriber.
event_types on a subscription is metadata used for future filtering; an empty list means the subscriber accepts all events.
Requests are unauthenticated (trusted internal network), matching the spec's silence on auth; no Secrets Manager secret is needed because no third-party credentials are used.
Region and resource names come from environment variables (AWS_REGION, SNS_TOPIC_ARN, queue URLs, table name) so the service can point at LocalStack via AWS_ENDPOINT_URL.
Event payloads are JSON objects under 256 KB, well within the SNS message size limit, so no S3 offload is required.

🐍 Generated application code (initial): 7 files — FastAPI notification hub with a decoupled boto3 layer.

- `storage.py`: `NotificationRepository` wrapping SNS publish, SQS queue-attribute stats / receive / delete, and DynamoDB subscription CRUD. Clients are built by module-level factories that honour `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL` and default to `us-east-1`; topic ARN, queue URLs/names, table name and GSI all come from env vars with plan-matching defaults, with name-based resolution fallbacks. Errors are normalised to `NotFoundError` / `DependencyError` (no botocore import; AWS error codes read off `exc.response`).
- `models.py`: pydantic models (Channel enum → unknown channels yield 422), request/response envelopes, plus a v1/v2-safe `dump_model` helper.
- `app.py`: all ten planned endpoints, repository supplied through a FastAPI dependency (`get_repository`) so tests can override it; storage errors map to 404/502, target format validation returns 422, health returns 503 when a dependency check fails. Uvicorn entry binds 127.0.0.1 by default (Bandit-safe).
- `tests/test_app.py`: TestClient coverage of every endpoint (success, validation, 404, 502, degraded health) via an in-memory fake repository, plus storage-layer tests using stubbed SNS/SQS/DynamoDB objects monkeypatched over the client factories — completely offline.
- `conftest.py` makes the project root importable; `requirements.txt` lists only fastapi, uvicorn, boto3, pydantic; README documents endpoints, env config and how to run.

🏗️ Generated Terraform (initial): 4 files — Terraform for the notification hub, scoped exactly to the plan's aws_resources list.

Files:
- versions.tf: terraform block, required_version >= 1.3.0, hashicorp/aws pinned ~> 5.0.
- variables.tf: defaults match the plan's resource names (notification-hub-events-topic, notification-hub-email-queue, notification-hub-webhook-queue, notification-hub-dlq, notification-hub-subscriptions, notification-hub-service-role, /notification-hub/application).
- main.tf: provider with default_tags (project, managed-by, environment); customer-managed KMS key (rotation enabled, explicit key policy with no wildcard principals, statements for SNS/SQS and the CloudWatch Logs service principal) plus alias; SNS topic encrypted with the CMK; shared DLQ and two channel queues (email/webhook via for_each) all KMS-encrypted with redrive to the DLQ; per-queue SQS policies allowing only sns.amazonaws.com with an aws:SourceArn condition on the topic; SNS->SQS subscriptions with raw_message_delivery; DynamoDB table (PAY_PER_REQUEST, PITR on, SSE with the CMK, channel/created_at GSI); CloudWatch log group with retention and KMS encryption; IAM role (EC2 service principal, no wildcard trust) with a least-privilege policy — sns:Publish on the topic only, SQS read/delete on the three queue ARNs, DynamoDB CRUD/Query on the table and its named index, logs write on the specific log group, and kms:Decrypt/GenerateDataKey on the single key. No "*" resources or "*" actions in any IAM policy.
- outputs.tf: topic ARN/name, both channel queue URLs/ARNs plus a channel->URL map, DLQ URL/ARN, table name/ARN, GSI name, log group name, role/policy ARNs, KMS key ARN — everything the FastAPI app needs as env vars.

Only LocalStack Community services are used (SNS, SQS, DynamoDB, IAM, CloudWatch Logs, KMS); no Lambda, API Gateway, RDS, ECS, EKS or ElastiCache.
